source_text:
θεϊκῶς, ὁμοούσιον δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν τὸν αὐτὸν ἀνθρωπίνως. τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις
ἀναστρέψει Χριστὸς τοῦ καθ' ἑαυτὸν μυστηρίου τὴν γνῶσιν.
βʹ. Ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ τιμωμένη τε καὶ ἁγιαζομένη· ὅτι
γὰρ τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι, οὔτ' ἂν ἐδεήθη βαπτίσματος, οὔτε μὴν τοῦ Ἁγίου
Πνεύματος μετασχεῖν, μάλιστα μὲν ἀρκέσει πρὸς πληροφορίαν τὸ αὐτὸν εἶναι τοῦ
Πνεύματος χορηγόν.
thought_title: The humanity in Christ was honored and sanctified
orientation: Cyril is addressing Theodore of Mopsuestia, arguing that the same Christ is consubstantial with the Father divinely and with us humanly, and that those who think rightly will have Christ reveal the mystery to them.
pass_a_gloss: divinely, and consubstantial also with us the same one humanly. To those who have chosen to think in this way Christ will reveal the knowledge of the mystery concerning himself. For the nature of the human being in Christ was being honored and sanctified; for as far as concerns being, he would not have needed baptism, nor indeed to share in the Holy Spirit; for complete proof it will be enough above all that he himself is the giver of the Spirit.

choices.why: The verb ἀναστρέφω in this context means to turn back or disclose, and 'reveal' fits the sense of Christ making known the knowledge of the mystery.

choices.term: τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι
choices.why: This idiomatic phrase means 'as far as it pertains to existence' or 'with regard to his being'; the rendering keeps the literal force of ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι.
rejected: as far as it came to be
in respect of coming into being

choices.why: Πληροφορία here means full assurance or complete conviction; 'complete proof' captures the sense of sufficient evidence for certainty.
The glossary fixes χορηγός as 'giver' for the one who supplies or bestows the Spirit.

pass_b_english: Divinely, consubstantial with the Father; and with us, the same one humanly. To those chosen to think thus Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery. For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified. For as far as his own being is concerned, he would not have needed baptism, nor indeed to share in the Holy Spirit. Most of all it will suffice for full assurance that he himself is the giver of the Spirit.

problems.quote: For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified.
problems.source_quote: Ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ τιμωμένη τε καὶ ἁγιαζομένη· ὅτι γὰρ τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι
problems.why: The English drops the opening 'For' (γὰρ) that connects this to the preceding thought about Christ revealing the mystery to those who think rightly.
problems.fix: For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified. For as far as concerns his being...

problems.source_quote: τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι
problems.why: Source says 'the one who came to be', i.e., the Word who came into existence as man, not 'his being' abstractly.
problems.fix: the one who came to be
problems.ruling: τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι = 'as far as concerns coming into existence/being born', referring to Christ's becoming man, not abstract 'his being'

problems.quote: For complete proof it will be enough above all
problems.why: μάλιστα μὲν means 'above all'/'most of all' but the syntax shows this is the primary argument, not 'complete proof'; πληροφορίαν is 'full assurance'/'conviction', not 'proof'.
problems.fix: most of all it will suffice for full assurance that he himself is the giver of the Spirit.
problems.ruling: πληροφορίαν means 'full assurance/conviction', not 'proof'; mistranslates meaning, misleading reader.

edits.old: For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified.
edits.new: For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified. For

edits.old: As far as concerns his being,
edits.new: As far as concerns the one who came to be,

edits.old: For complete proof it will be enough above all
edits.new: Most of all it will suffice for full assurance

problems.quote: the one who came to be
problems.source_quote: τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι
problems.why: τὸ ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι = 'as far as concerns being/existence,' not 'the one who came to be.' Misreads impersonal construction as personal.
problems.fix: as far as his own being is concerned

problems.quote: For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified.
problems.source_quote: θεϊκῶς, ὁμοούσιον δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν τὸν αὐτὸν ἀνθρωπίνως. τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις ἀναστρέψει Χριστὸς τοῦ καθ' ἑαυτὸν μυστηρίου τὴν γνῶσιν.
problems.why: Entire opening sentence omitted: Christ consubstantial with Father divinely, with us humanly; he will reveal knowledge of his mystery to those so minded.
problems.fix: Divinely, consubstantial with the Father; and with us, the same one humanly. To those chosen to think thus Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery.
problems.ruling: Major omission: entire opening sentence about Christ's dual nature (θεϊκῶς/ὁμοούσιον/ἀνθρωπίνως) and mystery revelation lost.

edits.old: For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified. For As far as concerns the one who came to be,
edits.new: Divinely, consubstantial with the Father; and with us, the same one humanly. To those chosen to think thus Christ will reveal the knowledge of his own mystery. For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified. For as far as his own being is concerned,

fixed: The mistranslation of 'τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι' is corrected to 'as far as his own being is concerned'.
The omitted opening sentence is restored.

last_rejected.quote: For the humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ τιμωμένη τε καὶ ἁγιαζομένη
last_rejected.why: Greek is a general truth ('the human nature in Christ is honored and sanctified'), not past progressive.
last_rejected.fix: For the human nature in Christ is honored and sanctified.
last_rejected.ruling: Ἦν is imperfect indicative, 'was being' is grammatically accurate; general truth vs. progressive is interpretive preference, not major error.

last_rejected.quote: Most of all it will suffice
last_rejected.why: μάλιστα μὲν means 'above all'/'especially,' not 'most of all' in sense of quantity.
last_rejected.fix: Above all, it will suffice for full assurance that he himself is the giver of the Spirit.
last_rejected.ruling: μάλιστα μὲν = 'most of all/above all'; 'most of all' is valid English for this, not a quantity error.

last_rejected.quote: consubstantial with the Father; and with us, the same one humanly
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁμοούσιον δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν τὸν αὐτὸν ἀνθρωπίνως
last_rejected.why: Missing 'the same one' (τὸν αὐτὸν) before 'humanly'—the identity of subject is lost.
last_rejected.fix: Divinely, consubstantial with the Father; and with us, the same one humanly.
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'the same one' rendering τὸν αὐτὸν; no omission. Claim contradicts the provided English text.
